question: Is the near-field puff field a frame-time bottleneck at all?
method: paired on/off, same URL/camera/spawn, ?qa=frozen + qa.step(300) x3 after a 60-frame warmup, wall clock via performance.now()
gpuAttribution: unmeasurable - no GPU timestamps in this harness; wall clock includes submission and back-pressure only
reasoning: Turning the whole puff field off changes frame time by less than measurement noise, and the field contributes at most ~10k triangles to a drawn frame because frustum culling keeps the out-of-view clouds out. Level A (detail 2 -> 1) and level B (drop flank lobes) therefore buy nothing measurable, and level B is already rejected on projected silhouette error. Level C (do not draw far clouds) is already free: frustum culling plus the boundary fade.
reopenIf: a GPU timestamp channel appears, or PUFF_COUNT/bank width grows enough that the field carries >30% of drawn triangles
